newsitem.title: USA: Olympics bomb probe focuses on duffel bag - paper.
newsitem.headline: Olympics bomb probe focuses on duffel bag - paper.

text.p: FBI agents were examining an olive-green duffel bag from an Army and Navy surpus store as part of their ongoing investigation into the Olympic park bombing, the Atlanta Journal-Constitution said on Friday.

Federal agents picked up the bag at a store in suburban Atlanta on Thursday, telling the store's owner they wanted to photograph it. The duffel bag, which sells for less than $30, was described as standard-issue for soldiers in the U.S. military.
Investigators have said the pipe bomb that exploded in Centennial Olympic Park on July 27, leaving two dead and more than 100 injured, was carried to the site in a green knapsack.
FBI officials in Atlanta were not immediately available to comment on the newspaper report.
Former Olympics security guard Richard Jewell has been the only named suspect in the park bomb investigation, although he has been charged with no crime.
Jewell, 33, was originally hailed as a hero for finding the bag containing the bomb and has steadfastly maintained his innocence since becoming a suspect.
Earlier this week, CBS News reported that the FBI investigation was focusing on a new suspect and several possible accomplices with no connection to Jewell whatsover.
Other news organisations subsequently said federal investigators had several new suspects including one with links to the citizens' militia movement.
The Journal-Constitution quoted representatives of militia groups in Georgia and Alabama on Friday as saying they have had no new contacts with FBI officials.
